text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a perf regression in prod since the scheduler rollout (~03:10 UTC). token/sec down ~30% on a subset of runtime pods. initial traces point to long warmup/drain in the continuous batcher and spikes on KV lock waits.

sre-bot: PROD alert: token/sec anomaly detected for cluster-rw-us-west-1 · affected deployment=runtime · alert_id=ALRT-4721

ian: ugh. any quick profiling (pprof/flame) or kernel fallback logs?

maria: pasting small log excerpts — lots of these lines around the slowdown:

```
[2026-02-28T03:12:17Z] batcher: drain_time=12.3ms warmup_delay=8.7ms batch_size=2
[2026-02-28T03:12:17Z] kvcache: KVLock wait=14.6ms reads=47 writes=3
[2026-02-28T03:12:17Z] kernel-select: chosen=generic_memcopy reason=small_seq_len fallback=true
```

maria: flamegraph gist: https://internal-gists/rw/fg/205678 (private) — shows big memcopy/host->device memcpy spikes.

tom: merged PR 2026-02-27T22:45 · refs/changes/PR-2145 scheduler:adaptive-prefetch heuristic · commit abcdef1234 — changed prefetch to be more aggressive for latency but reduced initial coalescing window.

ian: that change would make batches smaller at startup which could cause kernel selection to choose non-optimized path for short sequences. also more small batches -> more KV contention.

maria: exactly. KVLock contends during startup/drain and we see kernel fallback messages. reproduces on a staging replica when I replay the recent traffic shape.

jen: given this is a rollout-caused regression and it's affecting user-facing throughput, recommend blocking the rollout and reverting. marking rollout on-hold :no_entry_sign:

ops: running rollback job now — `kubectl rollout pause deployment/runtime -n prod` -> success. pausing the rollout group for today.

ian: can we bisect to the exact commit quickly? or do a targeted revert for the scheduler heuristic while we investigate a safer paramization.

tom: opened revert PR: https://internal-git/repo/rw/runtime/pulls/2152 reverting commit abcdef1234. PR title: revert(scheduler): revert adaptive-prefetch heuristic. request_review @eng-runtime.

ian: short-term mitigation options: 1) increase batcher warmup_ms to 200ms to allow larger coalescing, 2) lower scheduler.prefetch threshold, 3) force kernel hint to prefer optimized path for small seqs until we sort selection logic. any preference?

maria: applied hotfix config (warmup_ms=200) to two canary pods and restarted them. within 90s tokens/sec on those pods up ~12%, kv lock waits down noticeably.

sre-bot: Metrics update · canary runtime-1/2 token/sec: +11.8% after config change · avg_kvlock=3.2ms -> 1.1ms

tom: nice. approving revert PR and starting CI for it now.

ops: revert PR merged -> initiating rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime -n prod` (batch size 10%). watching.

maria: after the revert and rolling restarts, cluster-wide token/sec recovered to within 2% of baseline across all regions. leaving rollout on hold until postmortem + perf tests updated. :white_check_mark:

jen: filing perf postmortem and action items: PM-987 (root cause: scheduler prefetch change reduced initial coalescing window -> more small batches -> kernel fallback + KV lock contention). action items: add CI perf test for warmup traffic, add kernel-hint regression alert, make scheduler change gated behind perf flag.

ian: also will add a microbenchmark for kernel selection with short sequences to catch future fallbacks.

maria: thanks y'all. keeping this thread as the runbook. we'll attach pprof snapshots and the bisect log to PM-987.
